analysis:
Both changed files are CI test scripts (scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py, scripts/test-provider-release-pipeline.py). They hold no provider runtime, attestation, key or consumer-data code. They change what the tests assert about the workflows, not the workflows themselves.

CI workflow test: head lines 883-951 now assert the build jobs run only when `inputs.<lane> == 'true'`. The push-refresh-caches path is dropped. Cache saves remain gated on SAVE_CACHES, which is true only for pushes to master. The strict-cache tier for master is still asserted (1031-1038). Checkout steps keep `persist-credentials: false`, the unsafe-.git validation tests (hooks, fsmonitor, includes, symlinks) are intact, and every cache step is still required to carry the CACHE_GATE condition. Nothing weakens the supply-chain assertions. Cache-poisoning risk from PR-scoped saves stays covered by test_only_pushes_to_master_and_dev_save_caches.

Release-pipeline test patch: the warm workflow now has a scheduled trigger (cron) and a `gate` job. The new test runs the gate script against a stubbed `gh` and checks the following. A transient API failure runs the warm (fail open). Skipped runs are ignored. A warm older than 6 days forces a refresh. A diverged or malformed compare result runs the warm. The test asserts the workflow must not trigger on `branches: [master]` and that `cancel-in-progress: true` is set. The warm still runs only for pull_request or refs/heads/master.

The actual warm workflow YAML and the gate script's permissions or token scope are not in the supplied units. Whether the new scheduled trigger weakens the PR-cannot-seed-the-default-branch invariant is therefore not verifiable here, though the test asserts that invariant. The DEV_CALLER assertion was loosened from a path-list entry to a substring match; that is a weaker test, not a security regression.

No threat-model assets (A-001..A-020) or trust boundaries are affected. No findings.
